q: The war between the Bahmani and Vijayanagara rulers started during whose rule?
explanation:
Most keys for 'the war started': Bukka I (first war 1362-67). Where Bukka I is not offered ('conflict began'), the key is Harihara I, in whose reign the Bahmani kingdom was founded (1347).
The first Bahmani-Vijayanagara war was fought under Bukka I against Muhammad Shah I (1362-67: Mudgal, Kautalam, Adoni). The rivalry itself dates from the Bahmani founding in 1347 under Harihara I, which is why other versions key Harihara I.

notes.text: - **First war:** under **Bukka I** against **Muhammad Shah I** (1362-67; Mudgal, Kautalam, Adoni) – where both Harihara I and Bukka I are offered for "the **war** started", key **Bukka I** (APPSC); treaty to spare civilians.

q: Who is the author of "Jaimini Bharatam"?
explanation: Jaimini Bharatam was written by Pillalamarri Pina Veerabhadrudu, a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha. Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam; Jaimini Maharshi is the sage of the original story.

q: What was the name of Achyutaraya's Sabha Bhavana (assembly hall)?
explanation: Achyutaraya's assembly hall was the Venkatavilasa Mantapam (he was a devotee of Venkateswara), while Krishnadevaraya's was the Bhuvana Vijayam.

notes.text: - **Assembly hall:** Achyutaraya's sabha = **Venkatavilasa Mantapam** (AP History PYQ); Krishnadevaraya's = **Bhuvana Vijayam**. (NextGen also has Venkatapati II's literary meets at "Venkatapati Vilasam".)

q: What was the military administration (department) of the Vijayanagara period called?
explanation: Kandachara was the military (defence) department of Vijayanagara, headed by the Senapati / Dalavayi; Athavane was revenue, Dharmasana justice and Bhandara the treasury.

notes.text: - **Kandachara dealt with military affairs / defence** – asked ×7 (APPSC G2 2019; G2 Mains; SI 2016; AP History PYQ ×3; G2 PYQ). Not revenue, finance, land survey (Bhoomi Sisthu), police, justice or religious institutions; **Athavana** = revenue, **Dandaniti** / **Mansabdari** are distractors.

q: Who is the President of the Imperial Council of Vijayanagara Empire?
explanation:
Most keys: Prime Minister. Strictly the PM's own title was Sabhanayaka, so option (b) names the same office (NextGen p.28).
The council of ministers was presided over by the Prime Minister (Mahapradhani / Sarva Sirah Pradhani), who was also called Sabhanayaka; the king was advised by the council, not its president.

notes.text: - **President of the imperial council:** the **Prime Minister** (AMVI 2009) – "Sabhanayaka" is only another name of the same office; the king was advised by, not president of, the council.

q: What was the administrative unit of the Vijayanagara Empire?
explanation: The question means the administrative system of the empire: the Amaranayaka (Amara-Nayankara) system, in which military governors (Nayakas) held amarams for salary and army expenses.

notes.text: - **Administrative system (G1 2007):** the **Amaranayaka** (Amara-Nayankara) system – a military governor (Nayaka) given amarams for salary and army expenses.

q: The Vijayanagar King who totally withdrew the marriage tax was:
explanation:
Most books and keys (Rocket, NextGen previous papers, APPSC G1 2010): Krishnadevaraya. Some keys and the old notes: Sadasiva Raya.
The king who totally withdrew the marriage tax is Krishnadevaraya (it was first remitted under Saluva Narasimha). The Sadasiva-period (Rama Raya) inscriptions record the remission of the barbers' tax, not the marriage tax. (Printed key Sadasivaraya.)

notes.text: - **Marriage tax:** first remitted by **Saluva Narasimha**; **totally withdrawn by Krishnadevaraya** (Rocket; NextGen previous papers – APPSC G1 2010). ⚠ Some keys give Sadasiva Raya; Sadasiva's inscriptions (Rama Raya's regency) record the **barbers'** tax remission (at Kandoja's request).

q: What is "Meruka" a tax on?
explanation: Meruka was a tax on the sale and purchase of goods; Mera was the Ayagars' harvest share, and Magani/Metta were land classes.

notes.text: - **Meruka ≠ Mera:** Mera = the Ayagars' harvest share; Merulu = the Talari's grain gifts; Meruka = sale–purchase tax (not Magani/Metta land or export–import).

q: Vijayanagara king who completely abolished marriage tax?
explanation:
Most books and keys (Rocket, NextGen previous papers): Krishnadevaraya. Some keys and the old notes: Sadasiva Raya.
Krishnadevaraya totally withdrew the marriage tax (Kalyana Kanike); Sadasivaraya's regent Rama Raya remitted the barbers' (Mangali) tax.

notes.text: - **Marriage tax:** first remitted by **Saluva Narasimha**; **totally withdrawn by Krishnadevaraya** (Rocket; NextGen previous papers – APPSC G1 2010). ⚠ Some keys give Sadasiva Raya; Sadasiva's inscriptions (Rama Raya's regency) record the **barbers'** tax remission (at Kandoja's request).

q:
Match the following taxes:
List I

a. Navidadere

b. Melivamsam

c. Manevana

d. Tudimeya
List II

I. Tax on Marriage

II. Tax on Barbers

III. Tax on Ploughs

IV. Tax Houses
explanation: Navidadere = barbers' tax (II), Melivamsam = plough tax (III), Manevana = house tax (IV), Tudimeya = marriage tax (I): a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I - the only option with Navidadere-barbers and Manevana-houses.

notes.text: - **G1 match:** Navidadere–barbers, Melivamsam–ploughs, Manevana–houses, Tudimeya–marriage = **a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I**.

q: During the ancient and medieval days, Pradvivaka was an adviser to the king in:
explanation: The Pradvivaka was the king's adviser in the judiciary, interpreting legal texts; not military, revenue or espionage.

notes.text: - **Pradvivaka:** adviser to the king in the **judiciary**; judge who explained legal texts (APPSC G2 2019; G2 PYQ) – not military, revenue or espionage.

q: Which of the following scriptures was considered authoritative in the administration of justice during the Vijayanagara period?
explanation: Parasara Madhaviyam, Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was the authoritative law book of Vijayanagara; Amuktamalyada and the Arthashastra are statecraft works.

notes.text: - **Authoritative law book:** **Parasara Madhaviyam** – Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti (with Yajnavalkya) – not Amuktamalyada or the Arthashastra.

q: Police rights were sometimes sold in the Vijayanagara Empire. What was this called?
explanation: Under Padikaval, police rights were sold to individuals; Athavana was revenue and Kandachara the military department.

notes.text: - **Padikaval:** the system in which **police rights were sold** to individuals (AP History PYQ) – not Athavana or Kandachara.

q: In ancient medieval times Pradvivaka was the advisor to the king in this department?
explanation: The Pradvivaka was the chief judicial adviser to the king, interpreting Dharmashastra; not revenue, espionage or military.

notes.text: - **Pradvivaka:** adviser to the king in the **judiciary**; judge who explained legal texts (APPSC G2 2019; G2 PYQ) – not military, revenue or espionage.

q: While appointing 'Brahmins' as 'Karanams', Harihara I of the Vijayanagara Empire followed the appointment system of which of the following dynasties?
explanation: Harihara I appointed Brahmins as village Karanams on the Kakatiya pattern - the Sangama brothers had served the Kakatiya state, and Vijayanagara village administration (Ayagars, Karanam) continued the Kakatiya system.

notes.text: - **Brahmins as Karanams:** **Harihara I** followed the **Kakatiya** practice (APPSC Jr Asst) – the Sangamas inherited Kakatiya village administration.

q: Who was the repair and maintenance officer of forts in the Vijayanagara Empire?
explanation: The Parupatyagar, the king's officer of the nadu/sima, collected revenue and repaired and maintained forts. Gowda was a village/sthala head and Dandanayaka a commander.

notes.text: - **Parupatyagar:** the king's officer of the nadu/sima who **collected revenue** and **repaired and maintained forts** (AP History PYQ).
